trust.synthetic: All data in the demo is fictional. No real person, genome or Emirati Genome Programme data is used.
trust.frequencies: Carrier frequencies are labelled as illustrative until cited values are added.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.own: A couple member sees their own result always.
privacy.overlap: A partner's data is visible only for the overlap (genes both people carry), and only if both granted that sharing.
privacy.clinic: A clinic sees only what the user shares.
privacy.counsellor: A counsellor sees the brief and shared fields, and never sees raw results unless they are shared.
privacy.analyst: An analyst sees aggregates only (k-anonymity of at least 5), with no row-level data.
privacy.audit: Every access to results, shares, and consents is written to an audit log.
privacy.revoke: Consent revocation takes effect immediately and is shown to the user.
privacy.guest: Guest sessions are deleted after 24 hours.

ai.heading: How AI is used and limited
ai.role: This is education, decision support, and navigation. It never diagnoses, never recommends a reproductive decision, and never replaces a counsellor.
ai.inputs: The language model never sees genotypes, names, IDs, or free-text identifiers. It receives only a pre-built, de-identified fact-card ID list and the question text after PII scrubbing.
ai.limits: The language model does not write new medical content. It may classify intent, select an approved content block, or lightly rephrase an approved block at a stated reading level. Output must pass the verifier, or a fixed fallback is shown.
ai.human: Hard routes bypass the language model and go to a human.
ai.routes: Distress or self-harm language. Pregnancy termination questions. Religious rulings. Requests about another person's results. Blame. Diagnosis requests. Medication or treatment advice. Requests to decide for the user, including whether to marry. Legal or immigration questions. Minors.

review.heading: Who reviews content
review.status: Health information in RAFEEQ comes from approved content files, each marked as draft or clinician-reviewed.
review.draft: Content that has not yet been clinically reviewed is labelled “Educational content — not clinically validated”.

demo.title: Choose a demo profile
demo.intro: Each profile is a fictional couple that shows a different part of RAFEEQ. Choose one to open its dashboard.

P1.summary: First cousins who both carry a variant in the same gene, shown with a hearing-loss example.
P1.explore: How a shared carrier finding is explained, respectful language about related couples, and a route to counselling.

P2.summary: An unrelated couple. Each partner carries a variant in a different gene, and they share none.
P2.explore: Reassurance without false certainty, and what remaining risk means.

P3.summary: Only one partner carries a variant.
P3.explore: What a single carrier result means for a couple, and when counselling may help.

P4.summary: Both carry a variant in the same gene for a condition with an early-treatment pathway, shown with a spinal muscular atrophy example.
P4.explore: How time-sensitive situations are prioritised for professional support.

P5.summary: One partner has chosen not to share their results.
P5.explore: How privacy choices are respected while each person can still use their own information.

P6.summary: A result includes a variant of uncertain significance.
P6.explore: How uncertainty is explained without numbers, and why a professional review matters.

legal.title: Legal
legal.intro: This page describes how RAFEEQ talks about privacy, consent and medical limits. It is not a contract.
legal.notAdvice: Rafeeq does not provide medical advice, a diagnosis, or a decision about marriage or family.
legal.synthetic: The demo uses fictional example profiles. It does not use real personal genomes.
legal.privacy: The Trust centre explains how sharing, counselling and AI limits work in the demo.

why.heading: A screening result is only the beginning.
why.body: Genetic screening can provide valuable information, but understanding what that information means is just as important. A carrier finding, an inconclusive result, and a result with no relevant variant identified are different findings that require careful explanation.

needs.title: Understand individual findings
needs.body: Know what your own result says, what it does not say, and where uncertainty remains.

needs.title: Understand couple-level implications
needs.body: Learn why couple-level risk depends on both biological partners' relevant findings, not on one result alone.

needs.title: Access professional guidance
needs.body: Recognise when a qualified genetics professional should review a finding with you.

helps.heading: Clear explanations, careful sharing, human guidance.

cards.title: Understand
cards.body: Explore genetic screening concepts and learn what carrier status and inherited risk mean in straightforward language.

cards.title: Connect with confidence
cards.body: Choose whether to share relevant information with a partner. Sharing is controlled by explicit consent, not automatic family access.

cards.title: Speak with a professional
cards.body: Find information about genetic counselling and understand when a qualified professional should review a finding.

cards.title: Stay in control
cards.body: Manage permissions, review sharing activity, and decide how your information is used.

journey.heading: Six steps from information to informed choice.
steps: Choose whether to connect with a partner.

conditionsPreview.heading: Different conditions follow different patterns.
conditionsPreview.body: Examples include beta-thalassemia, sickle cell disease, spinal muscular atrophy and cystic fibrosis. These conditions can involve different genes and inheritance patterns, and not every condition follows the same risk model.

guidance.heading: Technology can explain. Professionals can guide.
guidance.body: Some genetic findings require more than a simple explanation. RAFEEQ encourages access to qualified genetics professionals when findings are complex, uncertain, or may significantly affect personal decisions.
guidance.imageAlt: A couple sitting with two healthcare professionals during a consultation in a bright clinic room. Stock photograph.

privacyBand.heading: Your genetic information belongs under your control.
privacyBand.body: Genetic information can be deeply personal. RAFEEQ is designed around consent, private-by-default access, clear permissions, and transparent information sharing.
points: Explicit, separate consent for each kind of sharing
No automatic partner or family access
A visible history of every sharing change
